source_class: user annotated rear photograph plus physical inner-post dimensions, prior DSI506 geometry, and FFC measurements
proposal: Mount the Pajoniiir-M1 custom mainboard directly to the four inner rear threaded-post locations on the display module, keeping the mainboard parallel to the display rear PCB.

mount_pattern.source: inner four DSI506 mounting locations identified in the dimensioned rear drawing and user annotated photograph
mount_pattern.board_hole_pattern_policy: Use this exact 58 x 49 mm four-hole datum as the preferred display-relative mainboard mounting pattern once thread, screw engagement and coplanarity are confirmed.

z_stack_candidate.status: GEOMETRICALLY_LOCKED_FROM_PHYSICAL_H5_AND_PRIOR_Z5_DATUM; local component clearance still requires XY obstruction map
z_stack_candidate.cross_check: rear PCB Z=5 mm + measured post H=5 mm = post top Z=10 mm, consistent with prior C=10 mm front-glass-to-maximum-rear-feature measurement

ffc.routing_concept: Use a controlled U-bend near the display right edge and place the M1 host DSI receptacle in the corresponding right-side region. The 60 mm cable is compatible in principle with a direct-behind-display layout, but host connector XY and bend radius remain physical-fit items.

mainboard_orientation_candidate.display_facing_side_policy: Keep substantially component-free because the nominal inter-board plane gap is only 5.0 mm and display-side obstructions consume part of that gap. The host DSI receptacle may be an intentional exception after local collision validation.
assembly_sequence_candidate: pre-insert FFC into the display-facing host receptacle if access requires it
seat mainboard directly on the four post tops at Z=10.0 mm
secure with verified thread, screw length and washer/head geometry
route the 60 x 15 mm Type-B FFC through the approved U-bend without twist or over-folding

why_preferred: Uses existing display-relative mechanical datums instead of introducing independent enclosure standoffs.
Locks the mainboard seating plane directly to the display at Z=10.0 mm.
Keeps display-to-mainboard alignment deterministic and repeatable.
Reduces enclosure complexity and tolerance stack-up.
The 58 x 49 mm pattern is central enough to support a mainboard larger than the pattern while still allowing connector overhang toward enclosure walls.
The display DSI receptacle is close to the right edge, which is favorable for a short controlled FFC return path to a directly mounted mainboard.
closed_or_partially_closed: post outside diameter = 5.00 mm physical measurement
post height above display rear PCB = 5.00 mm physical measurement
candidate mainboard rear copper plane = Z 11.60 mm for 1.6 mm PCB
FFC Type-B cable orientation and display receptacle approach/insertion direction
hard_gates_before_production_lock: confirm all four marked posts are available threaded mounting points and verify coplanarity with a flat test plate/PCB
confirm thread type; M2.5 is currently only a user estimate
measure usable thread depth / safe screw engagement
select mainboard mounting-hole diameter and screw head/washer geometry
confirm the display assembly tolerates added mainboard mass and screw preload without stressing the LCD stack
create a local XY obstruction map for display-side components within the 5 mm inter-board plane gap
validate the 60 mm FFC bend path and mating/removal keepout with the final host connector position
identify display receptacle pin 1 and prove host pin 1 to module pin 1 mapping
finalize enclosure walls and user-I/O connector datums before freezing the mainboard outline
do_not_infer: Do not production-lock M2.5 until a known screw or measured thread proves it.
Do not treat the 5 mm plane gap as universal component clearance; local display components reduce it.
Do not freeze the mainboard outline from the 58 x 49 mm hole pattern alone.
Do not place tall components on the display-facing side before the obstruction map is established.
